children: The US aerospace major has proposed manufacturing 48 of the 60 aircraft in India if its bid for the Indian Air Force programme succeeds

Lockheed Martin has proposed manufacturing 48 of the 60 medium transport aircraft sought by India in the country if it wins the $10.5 billion contract, with the US aerospace major also planning to expand its existing production partnership with Tata Advanced Systems or TASL.

India issued the tender in August to strengthen the Indian Air Force’s transport fleet and replace ageing aircraft. The programme covers aircraft with a payload capacity of 18-30 tonnes and requires them to operate from high-altitude and semi-prepared airfields. Five Indian companies, TASL, Mahindra Group, Adani Defence & Aerospace, Hindustan Aeronautics or HAL and Reliance Defence, are competing for the contract in partnership with international aircraft manufacturers.

Lockheed Martin has partnered with TASL for the bid. The US company already manufactures components and empennages, or tail assemblies, for its C-130J Super Hercules aircraft with Tata in Hyderabad, supplying the global aircraft programme.

Dan Tenney, Senior Vice President, Global Business Development and Strategy, Lockheed Martin, said the company plans to build on the existing Tata manufacturing relationship if its bid is successful. He said the existing production capability, which includes components and empennages for the C-130J, would be expanded under the current proposal, with further production and other activities planned in India.

The Tata-Lockheed Martin partnership currently includes production of C-130J empennages in Hyderabad for the aircraft's global supply chain. Tenney said the partnership had helped India develop advanced capabilities for the aircraft and could be expanded further if Lockheed Martin and TASL secure the contract.
48 Aircraft To Be Manufactured In India

Under Lockheed Martin's proposal, 12 aircraft would be delivered in flyaway condition, while 48 would be manufactured in India. The company has also proposed upgrading the Indian Air Force's existing fleet of 12 C-130J aircraft to the same advanced configuration. If implemented, the proposal would create a common fleet of 72 aircraft.

The Indian Air Force's C-130J fleet has accumulated more than 58,000 flight hours and has been used for various missions, including high-altitude operations in Ladakh, humanitarian assistance during the Nepal floods and the evacuation of Indian nationals from Sudan in 2023. The medium transport aircraft programme seeks aircraft in the 18-30 tonne payload category, with the ability to operate from high-altitude and semi-prepared airfields.

Lockheed Martin's C-130J-30 Super Hercules and Brazil-based Embraer's C-390 Millennium are among the aircraft being considered for the programme. Mahindra Group has partnered with Embraer for its bid. The C-130J-30 has a payload capacity of around 19-22 tonnes, depending on configuration, while the C-390 can carry up to 26 tonnes.

Airbus had earlier responded to India's requirement with the larger A400M Atlas. However, current reporting indicates that the aircraft is no longer being pursued as a main contender in the competition.
